Prevention: As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Do not allow pasture to be overgrazed or undergrazed
Supply multiple watering points to prevent livestock congregating
Monitoring: Scrambling, strongly-branched, annual shrub, 1-2 m tall
Stems: green or purple tinge; abundant, sharp, yellowish prickles; fine white hairs; angled cross- section; about 6 m long
Leaves: bright green; 4-9 pairs of pinnae, consisting of small leaflets which fold together when disturbed and at nightfall; 10-20 cm long
Flower heads: pinkish-violet; round, fluffy; found in leaf joints; about 1.2 cm wide
Check pastures and crops fields every two to four weeks, consider direct control if present
Check monthly for presence of the weed in wetlands and along waterways.
Direct Control: Wearing gloves, hand pull or hoe, or till the land, when weed is young/easier to remove:
Uproot at least twice a year (1. before flowering and seed setting. 2.
Just after the first showers when seedlings emerge)
Remove weed using hand-held hoe to a depth of 3-5 cm, at 4, 7, and 11 weeks after planting
Cut branches regularly, before seeding, alongside other methods.
Just slashing can leave fragments that regenerate
Corynespora cassiicola , are effective biological controls.
